source_text:
9.16 ̓Ενεπάγησαν ε θνη ἐν διαφθορᾷ ῃ ἐποίησαν·
ἐν παγίδι ταύτῃ ῃ ε κρυψαν, συ νελήφθη ὁ ποὺς αὐτῶν. Καὶ μὴν κατὰ τῆς ἀρετῆς,
ἀφθαρσίας λεγομένης, ὡς ἐν τῷ· ̔Η χάρις μετὰ τῶν ἀγαπώντων τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν
ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ· ἡ ἐναντίως ε χουσα κακία, λέγοιτο α ν εἰκό τως διαφθορὰ καὶ φθορά.
Ει ρηται γοῦν· Ει τις φθείρει, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ Θεός. Καὶ παρὰ τῷ προφήτῃ· Ενεκεν
ἀκαθαρσίας διεφθά ρηται φθορᾷ.
pass_a_gloss: Were-stuck nations in corruption which they-made; in snare this which they-hid, was-caught the foot of-them. And indeed against the virtue, of-incorruption being-called, as in the: The grace with the ones-loving the Lord of-us in incorruption; the oppositely having vice, would-be-said reasonably corruption and decay. It-has-been-said then: If anyone corrupts, will-corrupt this-one the God. And beside the prophet: Because-of uncleanness they-have-been-corrupted with-corruption.
pass_b_english: “Nations were stuck in the corruption they made; in this snare which they hid, their foot was caught” (Psalm 9:16).

And indeed, against virtue, which is called incorruption, as in: “Grace be with those who love our Lord in incorruption” (Ephesians 6:24), the vice that is oppositely disposed would reasonably be called corruption and decay. It has been said, then: “If anyone corrupts, God will corrupt this one” (1 Corinthians 3:17). And in the prophet: “Because of uncleanness they have been corrupted with corruption.”

choices.why: Set against ἀφθαρσία (virtue). Not ‘physical rotting of nations’ only.
